description: Real HTTP-header artifacts for the web-application-architecture module: a request tracing through the three tiers, the session/token state, and four clean/broken pairs for the EVALUATE-stage Diff-the-Trace assessment. Each header value is parsed by the `hdr` oracle (RFC 7239 Forwarded / RFC 6265 Set-Cookie / RFC 9111 Cache-Control) or the `jwt` oracle (RFC 7519); the discriminating field in each pair is the oracle's computed divergence over the real header bytes, never an answer key.

provenance.authored_with: RFC literal example values + a locally-minted real HS256 JWT
provenance.match: authored-with-citation (RFC literals) + computed (the JWT signature + the digest divergence)
cited: RFC 7239 §4 — Forwarded for=/by=/proto= forwarded-element (the literal example shape)
RFC 6265 §3.1 / §4.1.2 — Set-Cookie SID=31d4d96e407aad42; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly (the literal example) and its Secure/HttpOnly-stripped near-twin
RFC 9111 §5.2 / §5.1 — Cache-Control private, no-store (the sensitive-response control truth) vs public, max-age=300 + Age:142 (a cache served it)
RFC 7519 (JWT) / RFC 8725 §2.1 (alg:none) — the stateless Bearer token, minted this session with HMAC-SHA-256 over header.payload
provenance.honesty_note: Every header is a real RFC-literal value the `hdr` oracle parses per its RFC grammar; the JWT is a real three-segment token (HS256-signed; the alg:none twin is a real RFC 8725 §2.1 unprotected-token instance). The oracle's parse tree IS the answer key — the divergence in each pair (proto= present vs absent, Secure/HttpOnly present vs stripped, no-store vs a cached HIT) is the parser's computed difference, not a stored verdict.

pairs.control_claim: the app reads the CLIENT's protocol after upstream TLS termination (AU-3 provenance; SC-8 only if proto=https)

broken.label: Forwarded with no proto= (TLS truth unverifiable at the app)

pairs.control_claim: the session cookie is HTTPS-only and out of JavaScript's reach (SC-8 / CC6.7 / SC-23 session protection)

broken.label: Set-Cookie missing Secure + HttpOnly (the session gap)

pairs.control_claim: the /account response is never cached (SC-28-adjacent confidentiality at the edge; RFC 9111 private, no-store)

broken.label: public, max-age=300 + a cache served it (Age: 142)

pairs.control_claim: the stateless Bearer token is cryptographically signed (IA-2 / CC6.1; an alg:none token is unprotected)
